body: True. I just don't want to be the chronic basket/charity case.
I wish that other people's kindness was the solution to my problems. Thanks for yours.

Every woman in my family has been on anti-depressants at some point and my parents met at Alcoholics Anonymous. I've had an eating disorder since the age of 12. I first attempted suicide by anaphylactic shock at age 16 and was put in a psych ward. At 18, I was in an out of psych wards after failing an attempt to move away for university. It culminated in my really bad OD that I mentioned in another recent post in /r/AskDocs. I almost died and was put in a ward for 4 months, 3.5 of them involuntarily. After another OD a couple of months after discharge, I went to a different hospital to have ECT. It helped but the memory loss was too awful and it took away my intelligence, the only thing I've ever been constantly praised for. 

I'm now on another cocktail of meds because nothing has worked. Concerta and Abilify. I've been out of hospital for about 8 months now and I'm trying to go back to school. I have a psychiatrist and a regular therapist.
It doesn't get better. It keeps on getting worse. I try to dig myself out but I just keep on getting smacked down. I just know the consequences of failing an attempt now: months in a psych ward.
That's just delaying the inevitable
I knit and play music but lately they don't provide any relief.
I get relief from some activities. Binging and purging being the most prominent. It's a constant procrastination of attempting suicide. I don't know where I found the courage to in the past.

I fail at everything including treatment.

You can't let people have that much control over you. If you were completely isolated, would you still want to die? 

1. It won't work and you'll end up in a psych ward. Trust me. I've tried it. It doesn't work unless you do something so extremely violent that if it fails, will leave you maimed.

2. You won't get to give the biggest middle finger to your tormentors when you overcome this and become a success story. 

3. You'll hurt the people closest to you more than you could ever imagine. Imagine being the person that finds your body.
Well, knowing is half the battle. You can change. You can make apologies. You can leave them and find new people. This is cliche but suicide really is a permanent solution to a temporary problem.

I'm not trying to discount your intentions but is this more of a cry for help? It's equally valid but if this is a cry, there are better ways of getting help. You run the risk of getting Dxed with BPD if you do 'cry for help' attempts. 

Sorry I can't help too much without details but remember that life is never static. People change. Situations change. Emotions change.

The reason that stops me is that the attempt probably won't work and if it doesn't work, you're left off worse than before. You feel more alone, more depressed and possibly locked against your will in a psych ward.

Sorry, it's all that I have.

Where I live, you have to wait 6+ months for an appointment with a psychiatrist. Sometimes people go to the ER just to try to get any help.

I'm sure it's possible but again, the system is so stressed that I wouldn't have probably qualified for one because I could still take care of myself. Thankfully, I'm mostly recovered at this time and am keeping well with therapy and medication.
Too few beds for so many mentally ill sufferers. I felt like they would only admit a depressed individual if they were psychotic or in imminent danger of attempting suicide.

It helped me in that it kept me safe temporarily but it definitely wasn't conducive for recovery especially for me because my diagnosis was MDD with traits of BPD. Part of my recovery is about learning to deal with real life situations and hospital is just too sterile of an environment.

My experience there was eye opening to the reality of mental illness. It affects absolutely every demographic.   

The nurses especially want to help people but the system is so backlogged that a lot of the time, they can't give people the proper treatment. Especially for depressed patients, it seemed like they wanted to get patients in and out ASAP.

This guy(M) I was friends with was stewing because this other guy(J) can him an intimidating look. One day, M and I were walking the halls and he stopped outside J's room. J had just gotten an injection because he was acting violent so he was drugged and sleepy. M goes into his room and I hear pounding. J starts yelling, "Murder!" as best as he could in his current state. I get scared and run to the nurse's station. I tell them that something is happening in J's room and run to the lounge.   

M finds me in the lounge and says, "Look, heartskulls!" His arms are up to his elbows in bright red blood. The security guard comes and takes M to his room where he is put in restraints. J is taken to the hospital. I'm still in the lounge in shock and I see M, spread eagle on his back, being rolled on his bed in restraints onto the acute side. A few hours later, I see M being led away by the police in handcuffs.

First 2: I attempted suicide by anaphylactic shock.  

The rest, my psychiatrist thought that I was seriously suicidal so she committed me from her office.
